newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil edges up with futures, expiry muted.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil edges up with futures, expiry muted.

text.p: NWE gas oil gained ground on Wednesday as firmer futures propelled outright prices higher. Premiums were broadly steady in a market that took the expirty of the March contract in its stride.

April IPE gas oil closed $2.25 a tonne stronger at $167.25 after the March contract expired at midday. The delivery against March will be 148,200 tonnes with one party seen as the main supplier and up to ten parties the receivers.
"No one trader is taking a lion's share," said one dealer.
Heating oil barges traded early at March IPE flat for second half delivery and then at April IPE flat later.
Russian material was pegged around April IPE +1-2 cif ARA, in line with a 10,000 tonne lot sold at April IPE +$1.50 cif Germany.
A Russian cargo loading tomorrow was understood to be looking for April IPE +$3.
Russians had a busy day in the Mediterranean, a trio of cargoes selling at fob high quotes +25 cents for 19-23 loadings.

DIN gas oil grade was seen to be suffering from overactive talk. Bids of April IPE +$6.50 cif NWE and even $7.50 were heard for second half material, but several traders said these were "overhyped" numbers.
